subject: Climate & Environment
title: Best Before Doesn't Mean Bad After
description: A quick win: understand Best Before Doesn't Mean Bad After.

hook.text: Millions of perfectly good products are tossed because people confuse date labels with safety warnings.

buildup.text: 'Best before' means peak quality. 'Use by' indicates safety. Most people treat them the same.

discovery.text: In the UK, standardizing date labels could prevent 350,000 tons of food waste annually.

twist.text: Eggs, yogurt, and canned goods are often safe well beyond their printed dates.

climax.text: Some countries are removing best-before dates from long-lasting products to reduce confusion.

punchline.text: A label says 'best before.' Your nose says 'still perfectly fine.'

quiz.question: What does a 'best before' date indicate?
options: The food is unsafe after that date
The store must remove it by that date

details.summary: Date labels like best before, sell by, and use by confuse consumers into discarding safe food. Best before indicates peak quality, not safety. Studies suggest that date label confusion contributes to roughly 10 percent of food waste in Europe.
details.whyItMatters: Standardizing and clarifying date labels is a simple policy change that could prevent millions of tonnes of unnecessary food waste and associated emissions each year.
takeaways: Best before indicates quality, not safety
Date label confusion causes about 10 percent of EU food waste
Standardizing labels could prevent millions of tonnes of waste

faq.question: What is the difference between best before and use by?
faq.answer: Best before indicates when food is at peak quality but is still generally safe to eat after that date. Use by marks the last date food is considered safe to consume, typically applied to highly perishable items like raw meat and dairy.

faq.question: How can date label reform reduce food waste?
faq.answer: Eliminating or simplifying sell by and best before dates, educating consumers about what labels mean, and encouraging sensory checks before discarding food could all help. Some countries are already removing best before dates from long-lasting products like pasta and rice.
